claim: The memory exists and is correct. It is addressed by the WRONG THING. Measured on real episodes: learning from one episode reaches 0 of the next 4, because the signature includes the operand, and the operand changes every episode. Strip the operands and the same five episodes collapse to ONE address.
why_this_matters: This is the user's thesis tested as a mechanism rather than an opinion. 'Do it once and it is permanent' is exactly right; 'and it transfers' is exactly what the existing address prevents.

repository_finding.answer_memory_v1_own_docstring: 'AND IT WAS ALREADY SOLVED. experience_v1 records a recurring fact ... Nothing on the answer path read it.'
repository_finding.same_defect_again: experience_v1 is read by nothing on the MiniWob path either: grep of miniwob_actuator_v1.py and miniwob_repeat_v1.py returns zero references.

measurement.goals: five real goals from one task's five recorded episodes (email-inbox-reply)
measurement.cause: signature_of() includes every distinctive token, including the sender name and the quoted reply text

ceiling_from_todays_data_r174.reading: Memory can only act where the action VARIES. On 47 of 57 zero tasks the agent performed the same action on every rep and got the same failure -- there is no successful variant to remember. Memory's whole headroom today is 17 unstable tasks = 6.0 pp. The other 36.2 pp needs a written rule about a shape, which is what r172-r174 did.

conclusion.what_is_real: instant learning, permanence, and non-parametric memory are all real and already built in this repo
conclusion.what_is_wrong: the memory is addressed by the sentence, so it does not transfer across episodes of the same task; and no memory can help where the action never varied
conclusion.the_join_that_is_missing: a memory addressed by control SHAPE with operands stripped, written by the winning action path, read before dispatch
